title: METL can reach statewide operational use by deploying the sisal monitoring platform in **4** phased steps from baseline mapping to action
subtitle: A phased rollout turns the platform into an operating system: establish the sisal baseline first, then add monitoring, risk detection, and response workflows across the state.

blocks.title: Baseline acreage mapping gives METL the statewide sisal reference layer
blocks.body: Map where sisal sits across the state and organize the core geography for management. Evidence focus: parcel alignment, area delineation, district coverage, and a single baseline view.

blocks.title: Condition monitoring adds continuous crop performance visibility on top of the baseline
blocks.body: Track how mapped sisal changes over time instead of relying on periodic field checks. Evidence focus: repeat satellite refresh, crop-condition trends, comparative views, and exception spotting.

blocks.title: Risk alerting converts condition signals into early-warning management triggers
blocks.body: Flag where stress, weather exposure, or anomalous change needs attention before losses spread. Evidence focus: threshold-based alerts, hotspot identification, prioritization queues, and faster escalation.

blocks.title: Operational intervention closes the loop by directing state action to the highest-priority locations
blocks.body: Use alerts to target inspections, advisory support, and follow-up across the state. Evidence focus: intervention workflows, field-team routing, case tracking, and outcome review in one platform.
